intro: Every voice moment and character sound the original game plays, row by row: what the build maps, its engine hook (one named sound event per moment, aw_glut.c AW_SoundEvent; each one plays from the console with dbg sound MOMENT, docs/COMBAT.md Sound events), whether it has been heard in a build, and the proof. The reference for when a sound plays is OpenMW 0.51 as written down in docs/COMBAT.md, docs/ANIMATION.md and docs/NPC_VOICE_TABLE.md, and the builder's fallback test (tests/test_greeting_lut.py); the OpenMW source itself is not available on the build machine, so no row cites it line by line. Tribunal and Bloodmoon voices are out of scope until the expansions' NPCs are in the built world (NPC-VOICE-TABLE-ADDONS-54).
measured: The v0.0.57 release image's voice table, read back: 2,673 NPCs (2,675 from v0.0.58 with the two Orcs), every one with a voiced line (hit and attack 2,673, hello 2,648, idle, intruder, thief and flee 2,654); 396 creatures, every one with a sound (1,321 moments of their own, 1,760 by the shared fallback); 599 of the 601 sound records mapped; one named voice file the game data does not have (vo/d/f/Hit_DF007.mp3). Every build's report names what is not mapped: NPCs and creatures without a sound, creature moments, named sounds and sound records (the voice coverage line).

rows.proof: tests/aga_glut_test.c (every event resolves inside the table; a voice, a named sound and a creature moment played through the hook); tests/test_voice_features.py (every event is on this page); heard in FS-UAE on the Seyda Neen sandbox of 2 November 2026 at 32 MB Fast: the player's pain line, swish, armour hit, block, Health Damage, critical, punch, bow draw and shot, crossbow shot, thrown, projectile hit, Destruction and Restoration cast, Destruction hit and failure, knockdown, death, and an NPC's hello, idle, attack, taunt, hit and flee each played its mapped file (console log and a 103 s clip with sound); the creature moments need a creature aimed at, not in that scene; WinUAE not yet checked

rows.moment: The player's pain grunts and death line; the enemies' taunts
rows.mapped: the player's Hit line by his race and sex (id1/npc-voice-player.txt, tools/greeting_lut.py player_voices) when hurt (30 %) and when killed; the enemies' Attack lines on the fight start and new swings; hooks: dbg sound pain (always the player's own line) and dbg sound taunt. An approximation: the original filters the Hit infos with the player himself as speaker (race and sex, and also his class, faction, rank and the infos' other conditions); the voice table bakes each NPC's filter into its audience at build time and carries no race or sex condition, so AmiWind borrows the lines of the faction-less NPC of that race and sex with the commonest Hit set. It differs where a Hit info is limited to a class, a faction the player joins, or a condition on the speaker that the borrowed NPC passes and the player would not (or the reverse)
rows.proof: tests/test_greeting_lut.py, tests/aga_glut_test.c (a Breton man speaks a Breton man's lines); not yet heard in a build
